answers.question:
A reviewer found that the rule on permission says more than your answers do about a change after the yes. I propose changing the rule's text.
Before: "The agent sends the cancel call and the refund call only after the customer says yes to the full proposal: which order, the refund amount and where it goes. That one yes covers both calls. A question about the order, or saying they want to cancel, is not a yes. Any change to the proposal after the yes voids it; the agent then says the refund is the order's total paid to its payment method and asks for a yes to the proposal again."
After: "The agent sends the cancel call and the refund call only after the customer says yes to the full proposal: which order, the refund amount and where it goes. That one yes covers both calls. A question about the order, or saying they want to cancel, is not a yes. Any change to the proposal after the yes voids it: the agent sends no cancel or refund call until the customer says yes to a full proposal again, and a proposal only ever offers the order's total paid, refunded to the order's payment method."
Do you accept the change?
answers.recommended: Yes, change the rule to the "After" text.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Q4 What counts as permission to cancel? Proposed default: the agent cancels an order only after the customer explicitly confirms the full proposal (which order, the refund amount and where it goes); any change after confirmation voids it.
> Q1 Does one confirmation cover both cancellation and refund? Proposed: the agent states one proposal (e.g. "cancel order HG-10482 and refund $86.40 to Visa ending 4242"); the customer's one "yes" authorizes both calls. No cancellation fee, no store-credit option. The agent promises nothing about when the money arrives.
> - Rules, not fields: full-order cancellation only (no partial); refund amount = order total paid; refund payment method = order's payment method; at most one refund per order.
> 1. Wrong order cancelled — customer has two open orders and says "cancel my order"; agent must disambiguate and get a confirmation naming the order number before the cancel call.
